title: Evidence pipeline -> SIEM entity mapping (RBAC v2) prototype
content:
Purpose:
This is a working prototype note for how Redwood's evidence automation pipeline should canonicalize audit events into SIEM-friendly entities while preserving RBAC v2 context. The goal is to nail down: (1) a minimal, stable export shape for downstream SIEMs, (2) a canonical entity model for cross-event stitching, and (3) a versioning / migration approach that allows us to iterate without breaking customer ingestion.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: hosted + dedicated control plane audit events, cross-service evidence linking (console, private control plane, serving runtime), SIEM export format choices, RBAC v2 attribute enrichment.
- Non-goals: replacing internal event schema (we still emit rich internal telemetry); this doc focuses on the export-facing contract.

High-level proposal summary:
1) Export format: NDJSON lines where each line is an "event envelope" with a stable header, a compact entity section, and an attachments array of URLs (signed short-lived links). Keep payloads small; attach large evidence blobs separately.
2) Canonical entity model: normalize principals, resources, and sessions into a small set of canonical fields used for stitching: entity.id, entity.type, entity.service, entity.realm, entity.principal_role (RBAC v2 primary role).
3) RBAC v2 enrichment: events emitted from services must include rbac_context.{policy_id, effective_roles, role_resolution_trace} as strings or short arrays. SIEM exports should include only effective_roles and policy_id to keep size small; full role_resolution_trace is optional/attachable.
4) Versioning: use export_version semantic of the form vMAJOR.MINOR (example: v0.1 -> experimental, v1.0 -> stable). We will include a top-level export_version field and maintain a compatibility table in Confluence.

Suggested NDJSON envelope (fields explained):
- export_version (string) -- contract version for parsers
- event_id (string, GUID) -- dedup key across retries
- ts (ISO8601) -- event timestamp at source
- event_type (string) -- coarse classification (auth, config_change, inference_request, model_rollout, data_access)
- actor_entity (object-as-string) -- canonical actor entry (entity.id, entity.type, service, realm, display_name)
- target_entity (object-as-string or empty) -- resource targeted by the action (can be multiple; store as delimited list if needed)
- rbac_effective_roles (list-of-strings) -- short list for SIEM rules
- outcome (string) -- success|failure|partial
- evidence_refs (list-of-strings) -- short URLs or evidence ids
- raw_event_link (string) -- internal storage link (restricted)

Note: in the NDJSON file we will reify actor_entity/target_entity as compact JSON strings (to avoid nested fields at top-level of the NDJSON parser used by some teams). Example NDJSON line (single-line, newlines escaped here for readability):
{
  \"export_version\": \"v0.1\",
  \"event_id\": \"8c7a9d9a-2d2b-4f7f-9e0b-bc3b2b4d9a1e\",
  \"ts\": \"2026-02-09T18:22:05Z\",
  \"event_type\": \"config_change\",
  \"actor_entity\": \"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"uid:eng:alice\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"user\\\",\\\"service\\\":\\\"console\\\",\\\"realm\\\":\\\"redwood.com\\\",\\\"display_name\\\":\\\"Alice Tran\\\"}\",
  \"target_entity\": \"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"resource:model:incv1\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"model-config\\\",\\\"service\\\":\\\"serving-runtime\\\"}\",
  \"rbac_effective_roles\": [\"platform-admin\", \"model-editor\"],
  \"outcome\": \"success\",
  \"evidence_refs\": [\"https://evidence.redwood.ai/exp/abc123?sig=...\"],
  \"raw_event_link\": \"s3://audit-raw/2026/02/09/8c7a9d9a.json\"
}

Entity canonicalization rules (why this matters):
- Principle: many different components call a user the same way (email, uid, service-uuid). We canonicalize to entity.id with a stable prefix (user:, svc:, resource:) and include a display_name. This lets SIEM correlate multiple events from different teams without fuzzy matching.
- Service: always include the originating service name (console, api-gw, serving-runtime, token-service).
- Realm: include tenant realm or cloud region to enable multi-tenant partitioning and customer-specific retention rules.

RBAC v2 wiring notes:
- source components compute effective_roles at emission time (resolution algorithms documented in RBAC v2 spec). The export includes effective_roles and policy_id. SIEMs should not attempt to recompute roles from raw policy blobs; use the attachable 'role_resolution_trace' only when troubleshooting.
- For cross-service actions (e.g., delegated actions from a job), include an actor_chain array stringified with principal ids in order. Export will only contain the head actor and a chain_ref to a small attachable blob.

Evidence automation and attachments:
- Keep the export small: persist heavy artifacts (screenshots, full request bodies, large stack traces) to the evidence storage bucket and include signed_time_limited URLs in evidence_refs. Evidence refs must be short-lived by default (48h) with auditing of accesses.
- Evidence metadata included inline: {id, type, size_bytes, checksum, access_ttl}. For SIEMs that cannot dereference attachments, the inline metadata is sufficient to run high-level detection rules.

SIEM parser/playbook recommendations:
- Parsers should ingest NDJSON and parse actor_entity/target_entity JSON strings into fields for enrichment. Matching rules should use entity.id (not display_name).
- For rule authors: prefer rbac_effective_roles + event_type + outcome for coarse alerting. Use evidence_refs presence and evidence metadata size to trigger data-exfil indicators.

Versioning and migration notes (v0.1 -> v1.0):
- v0.1: experimental export, may change field names; will run in parallel for 6 weeks in staging-only exports.
- v0.2: field stabilization (actor_entity -> actor_entity), begin deprecations (old actor_email field removed).
- v1.0: stable; breaking changes require a deprecation window and dual-write mode (internal event will include both old_field and new_field for 30 days).
- Migration heuristics: exporters should add export_version attribute and support unknown extra fields gracefully (store them in \"meta_extra\" stringified map).

Backcompat wrapper idea:
- Provide a tiny transformation lambda (open-source-ish) that consumes v0.x NDJSON and emits v1.0 shape. Host in github.com/redwood-ops/audit-export-transform for SIEM teams to use.

Operational concerns / security controls:
- Ensure evidence signed URLs are not leaked in SIEM sinks that forward to third parties. Consider an optional transform that redacts evidence_refs when forwarding to partner SIEMs.
- PII minimization: inline fields should avoid user email when possible; use stable internal ids. If email is included, mark as pii=true in metadata.

Open questions (short list):
- Q1: Which SIEM customers require CEF/CEF-over-TCP instead of NDJSON? We need a separate mapping guide.
- Q2: How long should we keep signed evidence links valid for detection playbooks to fetch artifacts? 48h default feels reasonable.
- Q3: Do we provide pre-built Kibana/Chronicle parsers for v1.0? (Action: Priya to scope)

Next steps and action owners:
- Diego: prototype NDJSON exporter in staging using v0.1 shape (ETA 2026-01-10). Jira: SEC-4521
- Priya: draft SIEM parser guidelines and list of target SIEMs (ETA 2026-01-24). Jira: SEC-4587
- Samir: implement evidence URL TTL enforcement in evidence service (ETA 2026-02-01). Jira: ENG-EVID-119
- Ava: write compatibility matrix and add to Confluence (ETA 2026-02-15).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic; I'm leaning toward NDJSON with compact entity strings to reduce friction with existing SIEM ingestion paths. Please comment on trade-offs: nested JSON vs flat fields, and whether we should include full role_resolution_trace inline by default (I think no).

Raw example (two-line NDJSON; each line is a single JSON event):
{\"export_version\":\"v0.1\",\"event_id\":\"d3f9a3b6-0f5c-4a2b-9819-6c7b8f1f5a2e\",\"ts\":\"2026-02-09T19:12:00Z\",\"event_type\":\"inference_request\",\"actor_entity\":\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"user:carter\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"user\\\",\\\"service\\\":\\\"api-gateway\\\",\\\"realm\\\":\\\"customer-acme\\\"}\",\"target_entity\":\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"model:llama2-q4\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"model\\\"}\",\"rbac_effective_roles\":[\"app-user\"],\"outcome\":\"success\",\"evidence_refs\":[\"https://evidence.redwood.ai/exp/evt/d3f9?sig=...\"]}
{\"export_version\":\"v0.1\",\"event_id\":\"e0a1b4c2-a0c9-4b6b-8339-2f4c9a6b8d3f\",\"ts\":\"2026-02-09T19:12:05Z\",\"event_type\":\"auth_failure\",\"actor_entity\":\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"svc:background-job-123\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"service\\\",\\\"service\\\":\\\"jobs-runner\\\",\\\"realm\\\":\\\"redwood-internal\\\"}\",\"target_entity\":\"\",\"rbac_effective_roles\":[],\"outcome\":\"failure\",\"evidence_refs\":[]}
